title: The Relationship We Would Invent
hook: Name what you imported, then draft a few agreements you can picture this month.
steps: Two borrowed assumptions each, in a plain sentence: family, religion, culture, an app, an old relationship. Read them. Decline, keep, or mark examine. A decline is not a case against anyone's family. Keeping a form because you want it counts as design.

Four living agreements, pictureable this month and on a hard week: the greeting after time apart, a small repair, a celebration, and how you protect solitude. Behavior, not a slogan. A refused line is written down so it does not sneak back.
One tiny ritual for two weeks, plus the version for illness or no energy, and a review date. No forever stamp.
ending: Park the rest under later. A line you drop is part of the record.
pass: Either of you may mark sex, money, children, family contact, or public identity not tonight.
safety: Do not draft an agreement that polices a body, a phone, or a friendship.

title: The Future Memory
hook: Tell one happy scene as a memory, then look at the bridge back to this month.
steps: 10 minutes, past tense, a day that has not happened: a place, a line one of you said, a sensory detail, a feeling. Label it fiction-as-memory. Drop any scene that spends your partner as a corrected version of themselves.
Read it aloud. The listener does not fact-check the future. One sentence of what they heard. No grade, and no annexing the dream.
Then four practical lines: already true; must be built; a step this month; weather that cannot be forced, which often includes the other person's want.
Leave conflicting scenes side by side. Build only where you both say yes. A private hope can stay single-author.
ending: Liking it is complete. Building it takes a separate yes.
pass: You may offer only the step you control. Sex, children, relocation, or a proposal stays one possible future until they want it too.

title: What We Want More Of
hook: Start from appetite. Each more-of has to name a presence.
steps: 10 minutes. Up to five presences: a walk, a joke, quiet in the same room, a weekday ritual, rest. Keep something you can do at home on a tired day. Three honest lines are enough. One may stay private.
Before you read aloud, rewrite any blame into a positive action, or park it. Parked lines leave this card for a plain request. They do not come back in prettier verbs.

One texture question each, then stop. Pick one shared increase and one individual increase for a stated stretch. Two weeks is plenty. The individual one needs no labor from the other. A day can still be declined.
ending: Set a date to describe what happened. A smaller version, a window instead of a walk, still counts. No quota.
pass: Passing is allowed. A wish may bump a limit. The limit is real.
safety: Ongoing harm gets a direct conversation, not a sweeter verb.

title: The Relationship Bucket List
hook: Adventures, traditions, achievements, and goals that are ridiculous on purpose.
steps: Take turns adding one line, twelve or fewer. Tag each: adventure, tradition, achievement, or ridiculous. Cost in words: free, modest, or save-for.
At least two ridiculous and kind. A houseplant in a pet contest counts. Humiliation does not. At least two ordinary and repeatable. All four kinds, if you can manage that without padding.
If the labor all lands on one person, rewrite. Star one item or none. The star is not a vow, and nothing is overdue.
ending: Read the ridiculous lines. No laugh means fix or cut. End on one ordinary item. Retiring a line later is part of the list.
pass: Veto is allowed, and it can be dull and final. An individual hope can stay off the page.
safety: Harm is not a bonding tradition. The list pre-consents nothing about sex, other people, or a body.

title: A Promise I Actually Want to Keep
hook: One to three promises you would still keep if nobody thanked you.
steps: 10 minutes alone, in your own verbs. Keep only what you control, can do within a month, and would still want if nobody clapped. Cut anything grand, anything that polices their other relationships, and any promise of a feeling.
Optional second sentence: when this situation happens, I will do this. You may keep only the first sentence.

Read them. Your partner witnesses, may ask one question if the action is fuzzy, and stops. They do not enlarge it. A promise is not a vow the other person must match. One, three, or none tonight is allowed.
ending: Set a review date. A promise is kept, rewritten, or retired. Name a miss without a trial of character.
pass: Refuse to witness a promise that corners you. It goes back to be revised or dropped.
safety: Nobody may demand a promise in exchange for affection or safety. A promise about sex never binds the other person's body.
